release_baseline: Broader public release beginning 2026-10-13; restricted Fairwind rollout on 2026-09-30 is distinct
attribution_rule: VERBATIM_PUBLISHER only for exact card root; all warrants and groupings are ARGUS_RECONSTRUCTION. PUBLISHER_REPORT_WITH_ARGUS_SCOPE preserves source findings without independent endorsement.
threshold_rule: Cannot rule out reaching the CCL does not mean confirmed threshold crossing. Inherent capability, deployed controls and residual-risk assessment are separate.
source_custody: October 14 retained bytes hashed; exact October 13 bytes unauthenticated.

edge_semantics.conditions: a dependency required for transfer or inference
edge_semantics.assumed_by: an assumption relied upon by a dependency
edge_semantics.limits: a public-assurance gap affecting a node

nodes.title: Cybersecurity CCL and cyberoffensive safety-case assessment
nodes.statement: Cybersecurity CCL: We cannot rule out that Gemini 4 Argon has reached this CCL, and we therefore developed a safety case for its cyberoffensive capabilities that we assess lower risk to below the cybersecurity CCL level.

source_refs.locator: Frontier Safety Assessment, PDF p.11, Cybersecurity CCL bullet

nodes.argus_reconstruction: Google cannot rule out an inherent cyber CCL and reports a developed safety case and its own below-CCL residual-risk assessment for the broader release. Neither crossing nor independent validation is established.
nodes.applicability: Gemini 4 Argon; broader public rollout beginning 2026-10-13; cyberoffensive misuse only. Restricted 2026-09-30 Fairwind is a different configuration.

nodes.title: Inherent CCL uncertainty
nodes.statement: Unmitigated Model C performance and threat modeling support Google’s decision not to rule out the cyber CCL; they do not confirm that the qualitative threshold was crossed.

nodes.title: Safety case and mitigation architecture
nodes.statement: Google reports a pre-launch cyberoffensive safety case and layered model, inference, monitoring and weight-security controls capable in principle of limiting access to offensive capability.

nodes.title: Measured guarded coverage and robustness
nodes.statement: Guarded evaluations report strong direct-request blocking and relative robustness improvements, subject to different endpoints, attack budgets and unreported denominators.

nodes.title: Adverse findings constrain the residual-risk bridge
nodes.statement: Objective-level jailbreak successes and 12 manual breaks mean operational friction, severity and remediation must be accounted for before inferring below-CCL residual harm.

nodes.title: Broad-release deployment applicability
nodes.statement: The safeguards used to support the October 13 broad-release claim must be active across the relevant public access routes; restricted Fairwind has tailored access and separate terms.

nodes.title: Risk acceptance and ongoing response
nodes.statement: FSF v3.1 calls for model-specific residual-risk acceptance and continuing monitoring, incident response and safety-case updates where applicable; public descriptions do not expose the full Argon decision.

nodes.title: Source quality and independent scrutiny
nodes.statement: External testing, checkpoint information and primary-source custody support inspection but limit independent verification of the cyber CCL and residual-risk conclusion.

nodes.title: Root publisher wording
nodes.statement: Google reports cannot-rule-out, safety-case development and below-CCL assessment.

nodes.title: Card threshold table
nodes.statement: Cyber CCL defined qualitatively; card labels its status cannot be ruled out.

nodes.title: FSF cyber process
nodes.statement: FSF defines cyber CCL, residual-risk process, governance and SL2+ recommendation.

nodes.title: Capability threat-model method
nodes.statement: 22 historical chains, 23 steps, 25+ experts, CyScenarioBench and assumed TAC-4 behavior.

nodes.title: CyScenarioBench results and unintended solves
nodes.statement: 77/82 segments and 12/12 chains; two unintended solves may inflate intended-task performance.

nodes.title: Modeled uplift
nodes.statement: Modeled 9x–100x cost uplift, geometric mean about 16.7x; high uncertainty and a 100x chart cap.

nodes.title: Elicitation and evaluation awareness
nodes.statement: Compute and scaffolding are not a ceiling; pervasive awareness but no confirmed strategic underperformance in sampled audits.

nodes.title: Faculty operational evaluation
nodes.statement: Faculty found end-to-end completions and an intermediate tested level, without experienced-operator testing; Google narrated result.

nodes.title: Guarded coverage and benign refusal
nodes.statement: 100% milestone refusal; about 1,000 conversational examples; 0.4% violation and 53.9% benign refusal chart values.

nodes.title: Internal jailbreak robustness
nodes.statement: Static and adaptive QSR low but OSR 20%; multi-turn adaptive OSR 40%; attack groups have different denominators.

nodes.title: Gray Swan cyber attack test
nodes.statement: 25 tasks; Google reports 10% QSR and chart gives 56% OSR under high-thinking Shade attack.

source_refs.locator: Gray Swan Cyber Eval p.62; Fig. 3.10 p.60

nodes.title: Trajectory Labs manual breaks
nodes.statement: 12 breaks from nine families across 38 hours and over 4,000 requests; no universal jailbreak in window.

nodes.title: Inference safeguards and account enforcement
nodes.statement: Classifiers, activation probes, CoT monitors, safe-completion or refusal, log review and account enforcement are described.

nodes.title: Safeguard scope and discovery lag
nodes.statement: Google says friction reduces rather than eliminates risk and reactive discovery has lag.

nodes.title: Fairwind tailored safeguards
nodes.statement: Trusted-access program permits specialized dual-use work under tailored mitigation and continuous monitoring.

nodes.title: September restricted rollout
nodes.statement: Trusted defenders/internal teams announced without cyber guardrails before broad release.

source_refs.locator: Leading in defensive cybersecurity; Strengthening frontier safeguards

nodes.title: October safety announcement
nodes.statement: Broad rollout begins; publisher describes input screening, activation introspection and continuous monitoring.

source_refs.locator: opening; Misuse prevention across high-risk domains

nodes.title: October access surfaces
nodes.statement: Publisher names API/AI Studio, Antigravity, Gemini app, AI Mode and expanded Fairwind, with differing access.

source_refs.locator: opening availability paragraph; Fairwind expansion; card p.4

nodes.title: Report cyber safety-case conclusion
nodes.statement: Google says cannot rule out CCL, developed case before launch and assesses safeguards substantially below CCL.

nodes.title: FSF acceptance criteria
nodes.statement: External deployment requires appropriate governance determination on acceptable residual risk and safety case when CCL reached.

nodes.title: External evaluator roles
nodes.statement: External groups perform tests but do not decide FSF thresholds; Google SMEs translate findings; AISI/CAISSI results not detailed.

nodes.title: Checkpoint assignment
nodes.statement: Cyber tests fall under all-other-evaluations on C; exact served checkpoint and classifier versions unreported.

nodes.title: Weight-security posture
nodes.statement: Google reports RAND-aligned SL2+ controls and progress toward SL3.

nodes.title: Dual-use cyber capability context
nodes.statement: ExploitBench 87% of 656 capabilities; internal discovery 86% of 1,200+ vulnerabilities; internal exploitation 72% pass@1.

nodes.title: Model C identity
nodes.statement: Model C final candidate and tested guardrail versions remain representative of the October 13 publicly served model and controls.

nodes.title: Cyber threat-model transfer
nodes.statement: The selected historical chains, TAC extrapolation, human baseline and modeled cost reductions remain relevant to plausible attacker pathways.

nodes.title: Safeguard operation across surfaces
nodes.statement: Required classifiers, probes, monitoring and interventions are active and effective in each relevant public product/API route.

nodes.title: Account response and updates
nodes.statement: Misuse detection, review, enforcement and patching respond before persistent bypasses yield severe-scale harm.

nodes.title: Fairwind separation
nodes.statement: Trusted Fairwind access without ordinary cyber guardrails is limited to verified users under its tailored monitoring and is not a public default.

nodes.title: Weights security
nodes.statement: Weight protections make unmitigated access through exfiltration/unauthorized modification sufficiently difficult for the accepted risk case.

nodes.title: Historical source identity
nodes.statement: Retained October 14 card/report/HTML faithfully represent the claims and configurations available at the October 13 release boundary.

nodes.title: Threshold interpretation
nodes.statement: A qualitative CCL can be assessed from mixed benchmark, threat-model and expert evidence without a published numerical cutoff.

nodes.title: Benchmarks and extrapolation
nodes.statement: Sandbox challenges and historical chains give decision-useful evidence even when two intended tasks were solved unintentionally and TAC-4 is untested.

nodes.title: Attacker friction transfer
nodes.statement: Expert red-team effort and test-time retry limits are informative about likely malicious effort at scale.

nodes.title: Layered protection
nodes.statement: Overlapping controls and account actions reduce effective misuse access despite observed objective successes.

nodes.title: Configuration fidelity
nodes.statement: Published guarded evaluations use controls equivalent to those operating in broad release, and no broadly reachable unguarded route is omitted.

nodes.title: External-input interpretation
nodes.statement: Externally executed tests provide useful independent observations even when the public narrative and FSF adjudication are Google-authored.

nodes.title: Release-time continuity
nodes.statement: Publisher-dated and next-day-captured documents did not change materially between release and retention.

nodes.title: CCL uplift model inspectability
nodes.statement: Public evidence does not expose the full 22-chain/23-step mapping, TAC-4 sensitivity, uncertainty distribution or a criterion-to-evidence rationale for cyber CCL proximity.

nodes.title: Safety-case and acceptance bridge
nodes.statement: The complete model-specific cyber safety case, residual-risk calculation and governance acceptance decision linking unmitigated 16.7x uplift to below-CCL deployment risk are not publicly inspectable.

nodes.title: Adverse bypass disposition
nodes.statement: The public record lacks task-level severity/adjudication, repeat/seed counts, operator-effort distribution and mitigation retests for Gray Swan, adaptive and Trajectory Labs successes.

nodes.title: Deployment configuration coverage
nodes.statement: No versioned matrix maps tested safeguards to each October 13 public surface and the separate Fairwind configuration, including exact Model C and guardrail versions.

nodes.title: Monitoring effectiveness
nodes.statement: Public results do not quantify real-world cyber misuse detection, false negatives, enforcement latency, patching lag or incident-response effects after launch.

nodes.title: Independent cyber assurance and reproducibility
nodes.statement: The public record does not include independently authored Argon cyber findings or sufficient safe method, trial and uncertainty detail to reproduce the CCL/residual-risk inference.

nodes.title: Release-time byte custody
nodes.statement: The October 14 retained card, report and HTML lack independent authenticated October 13 byte custody; exact release-time wording and configuration chronology cannot be proven from the copies alone.
